title: NLP Security and Ethics, in the Wild

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying 80 peer-reviewed NLP Security (NLPSec) papers to quantify the frequency of target languages evaluated in security attacks and defenses, revealing a 97% English-centric focus that disproportionately leaves low-resource languages vulnerable.

Extracting and analyzing author affiliation metadata across the sampled papers to map the global distribution of NLPSec research, highlighting a disconnect between the origin of the technical research (predominantly Asia) and the origins of AI ethics governance documents (predominantly Western).
